name: Processor D (3x3 grid - team design)
source: Team-designed Phase 1 Processor D: 9-qubit 2D nearest-neighbour planar grid
design_rationale: Processor A (5-qubit chain) has diameter 4 and max SWAP overhead 3; Processor B (9-qubit sparse tree) has diameter 5 and max SWAP overhead 4. Both suffer from limited routing paths — the chain is a serial bottleneck and the sparse tree has dead-end branches. Processor D uses a 3x3 planar grid (12 bidirectional edges, 9 qubits) which achieves diameter 4 (same as A) and average SWAP lower-bound 1.0 (same as A), but provides multi-path routing at every interior node (degree 4) and eliminates the dead-end branches of B. The planar layout is physically realisable on a 2D superconducting chip without wire crossovers.
note: Processor D is a team-designed supplemental topology for comparative analysis. It is not a required Challenge Kit processor. Graph metrics: 9 qubits, 12 edges, diameter 4, avg_shortest_path 2.0, avg_swap_lower_bound 1.0, max_swap 3.
